description: Architectural rules for frontend component hierarchy, state immutability, container vs presentational separation, and API encapsulation.

rules.name: Zero Direct Network/API Calls in Presentational Components
rules.description: Prohibits invoking `fetch()`, `axios`, or direct HTTP client methods inside pure presentational / dumb UI components.
rules.rationale: Presentational components must be purely driven by props/inputs and output events, allowing effortless visual testing (Storybook) and UI reusability.
rules.remediation: Encapsulate network requests in dedicated API services, hooks, or Smart/Container components, passing data down via props/signals.

rules.name: Strict State Immutability
rules.description: Prohibits direct mutation of component state, stores, or signals arrays/objects (e.g. `state.items.push()`, `this.state.x = y`).
rules.rationale: Direct state mutation bypasses reactivity triggers, causes silent render bugs, and prevents change detection optimization.
rules.remediation: Use immutable update patterns (spread operators `[...arr]`, `{...obj}`, or immutable signal helpers like `.update(s => [...s, item])`).

rules.name: No Deep Prop Drilling (Max 2 Levels)
rules.description: Passing identical state or callbacks through more than two intermediate component layers without utilization is prohibited.
rules.rationale: Deep prop drilling tightly couples unrelated components and complicates refactoring.
rules.remediation: Use Context API, dedicated Angular Injectable Services/Signals, or a centralized state store.

rules.name: Mandatory Accessible Markup & Semantic HTML
rules.description: Interactive elements must use proper semantic HTML tags (e.g., `<button>` instead of `<div onClick=...>`) with accessibility attributes (`aria-label`, `alt`).
rules.rationale: Guarantees keyboard accessibility, screen reader compatibility, and compliance with WCAG standards.
rules.remediation: Replace clickable `<div>`/`<span>` with `<button>` and include required accessibility attributes.
